item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: Doing Multilingualism with Generative AI: Recentering the Users
item.description: Most research on AI and language tests what the model produces. This workshop asks what multilingual speakers do with it. Generative AI answers in dozens of languages, yet it organises them like a drop-down menu: one language at a time, each treated as uniform. Multilingual speakers move across languages, varieties and registers. What happens when the two meet? item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: Advances in Sociotonetics: Suprasegmental Variation in Tonal Languages
item.description: Sociotonetics is a young field at the intersection of tone phonetics and variationist sociolinguistics (Stanford 2008, Stanford & Yang 2023, and references therein). It explores suprasegmental variation in tonal languages, i.e. languages employing pitch distinctions for lexical and grammatical contrasts. Sociotonetic studies investigate both language-internal variation and contact-induced variation, as many tonal languages are spoken in multilingual environments. This is the first workshop
